answer: Delayed-Audit Reputation Ledger. Each new agent identity must wait a hollow grace period before its first payout clears, while the wait shortens toward a ceiling only as its record grows. Honest agents reach the fast zenith of trust after ordinary work; clones start at zero and stall. Every clone's accrued but unpaid balance also becomes forfeitable if a cross-check finds a shared audit ridge linking it to an existing identity. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the waiting cost and risks forfeiting all pending balances at once, making honest participation strictly cheaper.
